title: mqueue Module
content_markdown: The mqueue module offers a generic message queue system in shared memory for inter-process communication using the config file. One example of usage is to send time consuming operations to one or several timer processes that consumes items in the queue, without affecting SIP message handling in the socket-listening process. There can be many defined queues. Access to queued values is done via pseudo variables.

exported_parameters.name: db_url
exported_parameters.description: The URL to connect to database for loading values in mqueue table at start up and/or saving values at shutdown.
exported_parameters.example_code:
...
modparam("mqueue", "db\_url", "mysql://opensips:opensipsrw@localhost/opensips")

# Example of table in sqlite,
# you have the set the fields to support the length according
# to the data that will be present in the mqueue
CREATE TABLE mqueue\_name (
id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
key character varying(64) DEFAULT "" NOT NULL,
val character varying(4096) DEFAULT "" NOT NULL
);
...

exported_parameters.name: mqueue
exported_parameters.description:
Definition of a memory queue

Value must be a list of parameters: attr=value;...

Mandatory attributes:

* name: name of the queue.

Optional attributes:

* size: size of the queue. Specifies the maximum number of items in queue. If exceeded the oldest one is removed. If not set the queue will be limitless.
* dbmode: If set to 1, the content of the queue is written to database table when the SIP server is stopped (i.e., ensure persistency over restarts). If set to 2, it is written at shutdown but not read at startup. If set to 3, it is read at sartup but not written at shutdown. Default value is 0 (no db table interaction).
* addmode: how to add new (key,value) pairs.
    * 0: Will push all new (key,value) pairs at the end of the queue. (default)
    * 1: Will keep oldest (key,value) pair in the queue, based on the key.
    * 2: Will keep newest (key,value) pair in the queue, based on the key.

The parameter can be set many times, each holding the definition of one queue.

exported_functions.name: mq_add
exported_functions.description: Add a new item (key, value) in the queue. If max size of queue is exceeded, the oldest one is removed.

exported_functions.name: mq_fetch
exported_functions.description: Take oldest item from queue and fill $mqk(queue) and $mqv(queue) pseudo variables.

exported_functions.name: mq_pv_free
exported_functions.description: Free the item fetched in pseudo-variables. It is optional, a new fetch frees the previous values.

exported_functions.name: mq_size
exported_functions.description: Returns the current number of elements in the mqueue.

exported_mi_functions.name: mq_get_size
exported_mi_functions.description: Get the size of a memory queue.

exported_mi_functions.name: mq_fetch
exported_mi_functions.description: Fetch a key-value pair from a memory queue.

exported_mi_functions.name: mq_get_sizes
exported_mi_functions.description: Get the size for all memory queues.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $mqk(mqueue)
exported_pseudo_variables.description: The variable is read-only and returns the most recent item key fetched from the specified mqueue.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $mqv(mqueue)
exported_pseudo_variables.description: The variable is read-only and returns the most recent item value fetched from the specified mqueue.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $mq_size(mqueue)
exported_pseudo_variables.description: The variable is read-only and returns the size of the specified mqueue.
